rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> two-year split-plot field experiment at Ludhiana (2018, 2019) comparing subsurface drip, surface drip and flood irrigation with four weed-control sub-plot treatments. Q2: Tables 1<U+2013>4 and Results <U+2013> in 2018 total weed density at 30 DAS was lower under SSD than SD and flood, at 60 DAS flood had higher total weed density than SD and SSD, and total weed dry biomass at 60 DAS was lower under SSD and SD than flood (21, 36 vs 45 g/m2); in 2019 all irrigation methods were similar. Q7: Results and Discussion <U+2013> authors state that in 2019 no differential irrigation was applied because rain was sufficient and well distributed, hence irrigation methods showed no effect on weed density and biomass; weed suppression by drip appeared only in the drier year when differential irrigation was applied, and they conclude the approach is useful especially in years of deficit rainfall.
rows.notes: Study supports only the weed-growth part of the passage; it does not evaluate pests or fungus incidence, nor canopy dryness. Weed density and biomass were both obtained from quadrat sampling in the same plots (one method), so no triangulation. The mechanism (drier upper soil surface under SSD) is asserted/explained, not measured in relation to weeds; soil water was measured only for the water-balance ETa calculation. Single site, single crop, single soil, plot scale. Q7 is a judgement call: the rainfall/differential-irrigation condition is stated as the reason the effect was absent in 2019 rather than as an explicit requirement. Only Tukey letter groupings reported; no SD/SE/CI.
